examples.question_text:
Find these indefinite integrals.
(a) $\int 8\sin x\,dx$
(b) $\int -6\cos x\,dx$
(c) $\int 9\sec^{2}x\,dx$
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 8\sin x\,dx\\&=8\int\sin x\,dx\\&=-8\cos x+C\end{aligned}$

(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int -6\cos x\,dx\\&=-6\int\cos x\,dx\\&=-6\sin x+C\end{aligned}$

(c) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int 9\sec^{2}x\,dx\\&=9\int\sec^{2}x\,dx\\&=9\tan x+C\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\left(7\cos x-4\sin x+2\sec^{2}x\right)dx\\&=7\sin x-4(-\cos x)+2\tan x+C\\&=7\sin x+4\cos x+2\tan x+C\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate these definite integrals. Angles are in radians.
(a) $\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}3\cos x\,dx$
(b) $\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}2\sin x\,dx$
(c) $\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}5\sec^{2}x\,dx$
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}3\cos x\,dx\\&=\left[3\sin x\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\&=3\sin\frac{\pi}{6}-3\sin 0\\&=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$

(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}2\sin x\,dx\\&=\left[-2\cos x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\pi}\\&=-2\cos\pi-\left(-2\cos\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\\&=2+\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

(c) The interval $[0,\frac{\pi}{6}]$ contains no asymptote of $\sec^{2}x$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}5\sec^{2}x\,dx\\&=\left[5\tan x\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\&=5\tan\frac{\pi}{6}-5\tan 0\\&=\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A curve has gradient function $f'(x)=4\cos x-\sin x$ and passes through $(0,2)$. Find $f(x)$ and $f(\frac{\pi}{2})$.
A function satisfies $f''(x)=3\cos x$, $f'(0)=4$ and $f(0)=2$. Find $f(x)$.
examples.solution_text:
$f'(x)=3\sin x+C_{1}$

Use $f'(0)=4$.
$\begin{aligned}4&=3\sin 0+C_{1}\\C_{1}&=4\end{aligned}$

Integrate $f'(x)=3\sin x+4$.
$f(x)=-3\cos x+4x+C_{2}$

Use $f(0)=2$.
$\begin{aligned}2&=-3\cos 0+4(0)+C_{2}\\2&=-3+C_{2}\\C_{2}&=5\end{aligned}$

$f(x)=-3\cos x+4x+5$

coverage.summary: Authored six worked examples covering all six distinct accepted assessment methods with changed values and booklet-supported working. Assessments were classified only; their mathematics was neither changed nor re-audited. Questions and solutions remain separate editable fields, with single-dollar mathematics, authored continuation gutters and plain explanatory prose inheriting the renderer's blue. These analytical tasks need no diagrams. Independent review of the new examples and actual rendering verification remain for the coordinator.

examples.derivation: The primitives are -8 cos x + C, -6 sin x + C and 9 tan x + C. Differentiating gives 8 sin x, -6 cos x and 9 sec² x respectively. Source lines 1506–1508 and 1569–1594 support all three formulas and constant factors.
Termwise integration gives 7 sin x + 4 cos x + 2 tan x + C. Its derivative is 7 cos x - 4 sin x + 2 sec² x. Source lines 1624–1632 and 1685–1688 support integrating trigonometric sums.

For (a), [3 sin x] from 0 to π/6 gives 3/2. For (b), [-2 cos x] from π/6 to π gives 2 + √3. For (c), [5 tan x] from 0 to π/6 gives 5/√3 = 5√3/3; the closed interval avoids every secant asymptote. Source lines 1510–1511, 1528–1539 and 1597–1610 support the method.

Integrating 4 cos x - sin x gives f(x) = 4 sin x + cos x + C. The condition f(0) = 2 gives C = 1, so f(π/2) = 5. Differentiation and substitution confirm both results. Source lines 1624–1645 and 1690–1710 support the point condition and subsequent evaluation.

First integration gives f'(x) = 3 sin x + C₁; f'(0) = 4 gives C₁ = 4. Second integration gives f(x) = -3 cos x + 4x + C₂; f(0) = 2 gives C₂ = 5. The resulting function has second derivative 3 cos x and satisfies both conditions. Source lines 1714–1733 teach this sequence.
The supplied identity gives 5 tan² x = 5 sec² x - 5. Integration gives 5 tan x - 5x + C, whose derivative is 5(sec² x - 1) = 5 tan² x. Source lines 1748–1755 directly support this rewrite.
